title: Astronomical and calendar basis for the Passion chronology and the Chronomap's two-track time axis
question: What do modern astronomical and calendar reconstructions establish about the possible dates of the Passion between 26 and 36 CE: which years had a Friday 14 or 15 Nisan, how sensitive are the candidates (7 April 30 and 3 April 33) to observational versus calculated crescent visibility, intercalation and the Qumran/364-day calendar, and what follows for the reported darkness and the lunar-eclipse argument? Was a solar eclipse possible at Passover (full moon), and what does the 3 April 33 lunar eclipse actually show? The Chronomap displays two parallel Passion chronologies (Synoptic 15 Nisan vs Johannine 14 Nisan) and two candidate years; which astronomical statements are [A], which are [S]/[H], and where must the time axis display uncertainty rather than a single date?
why_now: Chapter 07 currently offers '7 April 30 or 3 April 33' as a bare pair and runs two parallel Passion chronologies. The time axis is a core display element, and the daily research run has not yet evaluated the astronomical or calendar evidence behind either date.
real_world_anchor: Astronomical and calendar reconstruction of 14/15 Nisan in 26–36 CE (JPL/NASA ephemerides, lunar and solar visibility criteria, Second Temple calendar scholarship).
novelty_reason: No previous topic covers the Chronomap's Passion chronology, Second Temple calendar reconstruction or the astronomical dating of 14/15 Nisan; the existing queue is about NOXIA's simulated time, cognition and physical systems.
